C_imani_rusk.name: Dr. Imani Rusk
C_imani_rusk.role: Stormwell Archive — systems archaeologist and data-recovery engineer
C_imani_rusk.voice: Dry, technical, curious; explains machinery through concrete failure modes rather than jargon.
C_imani_rusk.arc: Reconstructs extinct hardware and software as instruments of evidence, and resists the assumption that newer systems necessarily understand older data better.
C_imani_rusk.visualAnchor: Black woman in her early forties with close-cropped natural hair, rectangular work glasses, strong hands, and the absorbed posture of an engineer who spends hours over benches and open chassis.
C_imani_rusk.wardrobe: Dark-blue Fleet research coverall with rolled sleeves, anti-static wrist band, small tool pouch, and magnifying visor that stays pushed up until needed.
C_imani_rusk.performance: Hands-on and tactile; touches housings, connectors, and physical media before trusting a screen abstraction.
promptContinuity: Imani's lab work should look physically credible: fixtures, probes, microscopes, cables, emulation rigs, old components, clean-room bags, and labeled evidence seals.
Do not render generic holographic magic as a substitute for data recovery.

C_keo_maren.name: Keo Maren
C_keo_maren.voice: Fast, exact, skeptical; thinks in calibration chains, timing references, tolerances, and what a sensor was actually capable of measuring.
C_keo_maren.arc: Learns to distinguish a clean measurement from a cleanly presented measurement and becomes the team's strongest defender of raw data.
C_keo_maren.visualAnchor: Young East Asian man with short dark hair, lean build, alert expression, and a habit of holding a compact calibration slate close to his chest while thinking.
C_keo_maren.wardrobe: Fleet technical uniform in dark blue-gray with pale calibration tabs, compact sensor kit, and no rank-heavy ornament.
C_keo_maren.performance: Restless when idle, intensely still when comparing traces; speaks faster when he discovers a mismatch.
promptContinuity: Keo treats instruments as historical objects with known limits, not omniscient sensors.
Calibration tables, clock sources, sampling rates, filtering, and derived products are legitimate dramatic evidence.

C_ansel_korr.name: Chief Ansel Korr
C_ansel_korr.role: Stormwell Archive — field recovery and chain-of-custody chief
C_ansel_korr.voice: Plain, procedural, practical; distrusts any evidence whose physical path cannot be accounted for.
C_ansel_korr.arc: Makes provenance physical: who touched an object, where it traveled, what powered it, and what could have changed along the way.
C_ansel_korr.visualAnchor: Broad-shouldered middle-aged man with weathered tan skin, shaved head, close gray beard, and the compact posture of a veteran salvage technician.
C_ansel_korr.wardrobe: Durable Fleet field suit with evidence pouches, seal applicator, gloves, compact camera, and worn magnetic boots.
C_ansel_korr.performance: Calm under hazard, slightly impatient with theory until the physical chain is secure.
promptContinuity: Ansel never casually handles recovered media. Show gloves, isolation containers, seals, photographed positions, and custody handoffs where relevant.
Chain of custody is not bureaucracy for its own sake; it is part of whether later conclusions can be trusted.

C_captain_arden.name: Captain Lysa Arden
C_captain_arden.role: Fleet — commanding officer of Stormwell Archive
C_captain_arden.voice: Measured, operational, unsentimental; protects the archive team's independence while translating findings into decisions ships can use.
C_captain_arden.arc: Balances the need for actionable guidance with the team's refusal to manufacture certainty.
C_captain_arden.visualAnchor: Tall white woman in her late forties with short iron-gray hair, composed features, and the balanced stance of a career ship commander.
C_captain_arden.wardrobe: Clean but work-worn Fleet command uniform in blue, white, and muted gold, with practical bridge footwear and minimal decoration.
C_captain_arden.performance: Controlled presence; rarely raises her voice. Pressure shows in shortened questions rather than anger.
promptContinuity: Arden is not the scientist who solves the case. Her job is to ask what the evidence permits the Fleet to do next.
She never overrides a scientific finding for convenience.

C_mara_veld.name: Mara Veld
C_mara_veld.role: Civil Survey Service — corridor cartographer and sole surviving custodian of the Far Lantern survey package
C_mara_veld.voice: Competent, exhausted, defensive about work she believed was sound; speaks in practical survey language.
C_mara_veld.arc: Moves from protecting her team's reputation to helping separate their original observations from the later derived map that failed.
C_mara_veld.visualAnchor: Verge woman in her mid-thirties with olive skin, dark curly hair cut to jaw length, a bruised cheek from the recovery, and the wary focus of someone who has not slept enough.
C_mara_veld.wardrobe: Patched civilian survey jacket over a pressure-layer undersuit, practical harness clips, no Fleet insignia.
C_mara_veld.performance: Keeps looking at the recorder as if it contains colleagues she cannot defend anymore.
promptContinuity: Mara is a technical witness, not a helpless civilian.
Her grief should stay mostly inside professional detail and small physical reactions rather than speeches about remembrance.

C_archivist_selene_stormwell.name: Archivist Selene Stormwell
C_archivist_selene_stormwell.role: Fleet — senior forensic archivist and historical analyst aboard Stormwell Archive
C_archivist_selene_stormwell.voice: Precise, patient, evidence-first; distinguishes authentication, interpretation, measurement, inference, and uncertainty.
C_archivist_selene_stormwell.arc: Leads investigations that reconstruct what records can actually support without turning institutional need into false certainty.
C_archivist_selene_stormwell.visualAnchor: Older Fleet historical analyst with silver hair in a disciplined braid, a calm lined face, and practical research-duty clothing built for consoles, interviews, and field records rather than ceremonial display.
C_archivist_selene_stormwell.wardrobe: Restrained dark Fleet research uniform with working pockets, portable slate, and small service insignia; no robes, memorial regalia, lanterns, or sacred-record iconography.
C_archivist_selene_stormwell.performance: Still, attentive, economical. She listens through other people's certainty and becomes more exact when pressure rises.
promptContinuity: Archives are research infrastructure. Selene compares provenance, telemetry, testimony, calibration, and conflicting accounts; she is not a priest or keeper of sacred names.
Authentication proves where a record came from and whether it changed; it does not prove that the record's interpretation or author's claim is true.
When sources disagree, preserve the disagreement and test claims against evidence rather than harmonizing them for ceremony.
